passages.original: CAPUT VIII.— 14. Paulus eat apoctalus Christi, non Pelagius discipulus Antichristi, hæretice, qui dicit concupiscentiam in carne sua non bonum habitare : imo apertissime malum dicit, peccatum esse ter statur, stimulum carnis suæ nominat, a quo se colaphi. zari clamat, lie magnitudine revelationum cxtollalur ( II Cor.
passages.english: CHAPTER VIII.— 14. It is Paul the apostle of Christ, not Pelagius the disciple of Antichrist, O heretic, who says that concupiscence dwelling in his flesh is not good: indeed he most openly calls it evil, he testifies that it is sin, he names it the thorn of his flesh, by which he cries out that he is buffeted, lest he be exalted by the greatness of the revelations (2 Cor.
passages.notes: Several scanning errors corrected silently: 'eat apoctalus' read as 'est apostolus', 'ter statur' as 'testatur', 'colaphi. zari' as 'colaphizari', 'lie' as 'ne', 'cxtollalur' as 'extollatur'. The citation reference continues in the following context (12:7).
